data.title: China's gold imports said to have surged to record $209B through Oct.
data.description:
• China’s gold imports reportedly surged to a record $209B so far this year, in an unprecedented buying spree that followed a promise by top officials to make their country into the world’s marketplace instead of just its factory.
  • The shift began in January — the same month Vice Premier He Lifeng made that vow in front of a crowd at Davos — as the value and volume of bullion imports more than doubled from the month before.
  • Non-monetary gold purchases continued climbing in the 10 months through October, reaching a historical high that’s equivalent to nearly 8% of overall imports in the period, the latest data showed Friday, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Kalyan Jewellers shares jump 5% on news of Rs 2,000-crore fundraising talks with Warburg Pincus, other PE firms
data.description:
Shares of Kalyan Jewellers India surged nearly 5 percent on Monday, November 23, after a Moneycontrol report said the jewellery retailer was in talks with multiple private equity firms, including former investor Warburg Pincus, to raise close to Rs 2,000 crore through minority stake sales in its subsidiaries Candere and Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM).

Kalyan Jewellers shares were trading at Rs 668.7 apiece in morning trade, up 4.7 percent, making the stock one of the top midcap gainers. The company's market capitalisation exceeded Rs 69,000 crore. The stock has gained 37.8 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined 2.1 percent during the same period.

According to the Moneycontrol report, the proposed fundraising could mark Warburg Pincus's return as an investor in the Kalyan group, more than two years after the global private equity firm completed its exit from the listed jewellery retailer in August 2024.

Warburg Pincus had invested approximately Rs 1,700 crore in Kalyan Jewellers in two rounds between 2014 and 2017, supporting the company's expansion beyond South India into northern and western markets, as well as international markets.

  • Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

The latest discussions are aimed at accelerating the expansion of Candere and ATM, two brands catering to different segments of India's jewellery market.

The proposed investment could finance showroom expansion, inventory requirements, product development and brand-building as Kalyan seeks to capitalise on growing demand for lightweight, everyday and fashion-led jewellery while strengthening its traditional regional presence. For Candere, additional capital could accelerate the rollout of physical stores, while ATM could use the funds to expand across Tamil Nadu and potentially other regional markets.

However, the discussions remain preliminary, and the valuations, individual fundraising amounts and stakes proposed to be sold have not been ascertained, the report said.

The fundraising discussions come as Kalyan Jewellers pursues an asset-light expansion strategy through its franchise-owned, company-operated (FOCO) model. Under its FY27 guidance, the company expects its India showroom network to reach 426 outlets, with nearly 306 operating under the FOCO model.

Strong Q2 earnings support investor sentiment

The latest rally follows strong quarterly earnings reported earlier this month, when Kalyan Jewellers posted a 63.6 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 427 crore for the September quarter, compared with Rs 260.51 crore a year earlier. The reported profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 73 crore from the sale of a non-core land parcel. Excluding this gain, net profit stood at approximately Rs 354 crore, representing growth of nearly 36 percent.

Consolidated revenue rose 31.4 percent to Rs 10,323 crore from Rs 7,856 crore in the year-ago quarter, crossing the Rs 10,000-crore mark. Following the results, brokerage firm UBS maintained its Buy rating on Kalyan Jewellers, with a target price of Rs 900 per share.

data.title: ALS Ltd. H1 Profit Surges, Lifts FY27 Organic Revenue Growth View; But Stock Drops
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - ALS Limited (CPBLF, ALQ.AX), an Australian testing, inspection, and certification company, reported Monday significantly higher profit for its first half of fiscal 2027, with increased revenues. Further, the company raised fiscal 2027 organic growth view for Group and Minerals, but trimmed growth outlook for Life Sciences.

In Australia, the shares were losing around 13.41%, trading at $16.71.

In the first half, net profit after tax was $297.5 million, up 110% from last year's $141.7 million. The latest result included a $97.2 million non-cash fair value gain on the existing investment in Saudi Arabia.

Underlying net profit was $214.6 million, compared to $173.6 million a year ago. Underlying basic earnings per share increased 21.6% to 42.3 cents from prior year's 34.8 cents.

Underlying EBIT of $332.7 million climbed 18.6% from $280.5 million, and underlying EBIT margin expanded by 250 basis points to 19.4%. Margin expansion was driven by strong Commodities volume growth, pricing discipline, and continued cost control across both divisions, the company said.

Revenue of $1.72 billion grew 3.4% from last year's $1.66 billion. The growth was 9.6% on constant currency basis, with strong organic revenue growth in Commodities contrasting softer growth in Life Sciences.

Organic growth was 10.2% on a constant currency basis.

Further, the firm announced interim dividend of 23.3 cents per share, to be payable on December 21, to shareholders of record on December 1.

Looking ahead for fiscal 2027, the Group now targets high-single digit organic revenue growth and margin expansion.

The company previously expected mid to high single-digit organic revenue growth across the Group and margin expansion similar to prior year's improvement rate.

Minerals organic revenue growth would now be around 20%, compared to previous view of 13% to 15% increase. Life Sciences organic revenue growth is now expected at around 3%, with a return to mid-single digit growth in the second half. The previous view was improved mid-single digit organic revenue growth.

data.title: AI, caramba!
data.description:
A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee

It's been a bruising November for the AI faithful, with markets from Taiwan and South Korea to the US staring at steep monthly losses as the selloff in tech and chip stocks at the heart of the AI boom shows little sign of letting up.

Investors are questioning whether vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI tools will generate returns fast enough to repay lenders or big enough to justify some of the high stock prices.

Add to that the departure of Nvidia's influential figurehead Jensen Huang, an intensifying US-China tech war and the prospect of greater scrutiny over the data centre buildout following the Democrats' sweeping midterm victory, and the AI trade is looking increasingly shaky.

US futures bounced on Monday following last week's wipeout but selling pressure remained in Asia, with trading thinned by a holiday in Japan.

The scale of the selloff has once again caught the attention of policymakers in South Korea and Taiwan — the region's AI bellwethers.

South Korea's finance minister on Monday reiterated plans to stabilise the market, if necessary. Taiwan's financial regulator has ordered a tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China, stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

As Goldman Sachs' Tony Pasquariello puts it: "The market has shown its hand regarding its dependency on the AI story.

"After nearly four years of uninterrupted advancement — during which time the AI theme was rocket fuel for the market and, thus, the wealth effect — we've entered a far more complicated period."

The next key catalyst that could determine whether the selloff snowballs further will be Wednesday's release of the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge that could offer clues on how much further the Federal Reserve may need to raise rates.

Expectations of a 25-basis-point Fed hike next month have kept the dollar perched near a 19-month high, with the global stocks rout lending the greenback an additional safe-haven bid.

Separately, MSCI CEO Henry Fernandez conveyed a willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia's stock-market status in recent talks with President Prabowo Subianto, Bloomberg News reported, citing people with knowledge of the discussion.

Key developments that could influence markets on Monday:

- France, Germany, euro zone S&P flash manufacturing, services PMI (November)

- UK flash manufacturing, services PMI (November)

- New York Fed President John Williams speaks

data.title: Buy Chalet Hotels; target of Rs 1055: Prabhudas Lilladher
data.description:
Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Chalet Hotels

We attended CHALET IN’s investor day and visited the recently renovated and rebranded properties at Navi Mumbai and Khandala. ATHIVA Pulse, Navi Mumbai and ATHIVA, Resort & Spa, Khandala have seen an ARR increase of ~20-25%/~2x, after renovation and rebranding. ATHIVA pulse, Navi Mumbai has the largest in-hotel gym in Navi Mumbai, spa, salon, sky ball courts, pool and 30K sq ft dedicated for wellness. On the other hand, ATHIVA Resort & Spa, Khandala is an experiential property with mountain and valley views. CHALET IN is trying to position “ATHIVA” as a premium hospitality brand and both the properties we visited had a touch of elegance. Decision to have standardization (anytime breakfast, binge box, local immersions) across properties indicates CHALET IN is on the right track to position ATHIVA as a brand. CHALET IN has underperformed over the last 1-year amid flat international demand due to ME crisis, ongoing construction work at Powai and renovation/rebranding at Navi Mumbai. As noisy work at Powai is largely over and the Navi Mumbai property has been rebranded as ATHIVA, we expect occupancy levels to improve in 2HFY27E. Aided by recovery in MMR region and addition of two marquee assets (Taj, Delhi and Tower2, Powai) by next year, we expect sales/EBITDA CAGR of 17%/19% over FY26-FY29E.

Outlook

We maintain BUY with a TP of INR1,055 as we value the hotel business at 18x Sep-28E EBITDA (no change in target multiple), annuity portfolio at a cap rate of 8.5% and the residential project at NAV of INR17 per share.

data.title: MSCI reportedly discussed avoiding Indonesia downgrade with Prabowo, Dalio
data.description:
Key points:
  • MSCI Inc.  CEO Henry Fernandez conveyed a willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia’s stock-market status in recent direct talks with President Prabowo Subianto, Bloomberg reported.
  • Fernandez and Prabowo spoke for more than an hour on a Nov. 10 conference call brokered by Ray Dalio, the billionaire founder of hedge fund Bridgewater Associates, the report said.
  • Dalio, who has acted as an informal adviser to Prabowo’s government, joined the call, as did Rosan Roeslani, the CEO of the Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara. A few other minders and close aides were also dialed in, the report added.
  • Indonesia faces scrutiny from MSCI after the global index provider ​warned the country's stocks could be removed from its indexes in 2027 ‌and ⁠the market relegated two steps down from an emerging market to "standalone" status, bypassing the frontier rating.
  • Fernandez said during ​the call ⁠that MSCI did not necessarily intend to downgrade Indonesia and instead would continue to advise Indonesian officials on the ⁠steps ​they would need to take to ​ensure they meet the necessary standards, according to the report.

data.title: Bitcoin reclaims $61,000 after weekend crash: Can the recovery hold
data.description:
Bitcoin recovered above the $61,000 mark on Monday, November 23, after a sharp weekend sell-off pushed the world's largest cryptocurrency close to $55,000, its lowest level in nearly two years.

The rebound suggests some buying interest has returned after the steep correction, although experts caution that it may be too early to call it a sustained recovery.

The recovery has also been uneven across the broader cryptocurrency market.

Ethereum gained around 2% over the past 24 hours to trade above $1,700, while Solana also recovered modestly. XRP, however, remained under pressure, indicating that buying interest has not yet spread consistently across major digital assets.

What is driving Bitcoin's recovery?

The rebound follows a significant unwinding of leveraged positions in the crypto market. According to CoinSwitch Markets Desk, the recent sell-off triggered around $1.8 billion in leveraged liquidations, including a substantial amount of long positions.

The closure of these positions may have eased some of the forced selling pressure, allowing prices to stabilise and recover.

Vikas Gupta, Country Manager – India, Bybit, said Bitcoin's recovery above $60,000 reflected renewed buying activity and improving short-term sentiment after the sharp correction. He also pointed to the unwinding of leveraged positions as a factor that helped the market stabilise.

However, the recovery is taking place against a backdrop of cautious institutional participation.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have continued to see outflows.

Prateek Gupta, Head of Business at Mudrex, noted that these funds recorded nearly $1.8 billion in outflows last week, marking the third consecutive week of withdrawals exceeding $1 billion.

Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus, also highlighted continued ETF withdrawals as a sign that the rebound has yet to attract consistent institutional demand.

Why the recovery may remain fragile

Broader financial market weakness is another factor investors are watching. Concerns over US technology stocks, elevated bond yields and uncertainty around the Federal Reserve's interest-rate outlook have weighed on risk appetite.

Crypto assets, which are generally considered risk-sensitive investments, can face pressure when investors become more cautious about holding volatile assets.

Purvang Mashru, Lead Analyst at BitDelta India, said the increase in crypto trading activity needs to be assessed carefully. While decentralised spot trading turnover increased on November 22, the rise was largely driven by BNB Chain, rather than a broad-based increase in activity across major blockchain networks.

He said wider participation across the market would provide stronger evidence of a more sustainable recovery.

What should investors watch next?

The immediate focus is on upcoming US inflation data, particularly the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index due on November 25. The reading could influence expectations around the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decisions and, in turn, investor appetite for riskier assets.

ETF flows, the performance of US technology stocks and broader global market sentiment will also remain important indicators.

Riya Sehgal, Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, said Bitcoin faces resistance around $60,600-$61,200, with a stronger hurdle near $62,900. The $58,000-$59,000 range remains an important support zone.

She cautioned that unless Bitcoin moves decisively above the higher resistance level, the current recovery could remain a relief rally rather than signal a confirmed bullish reversal.

data.title: L&T will deploy additional NVIDIA B300 GPUs at Chennai Data Center via 'large' order; Details here
data.description:
Larsen and Toubro (L&T) on Monday, November 23, said Vyomai.AI, via its AI infrastructure subsidiary LTN Compute, won a "large" order to deploy an AI cluster.

L&T classifies orders in the ₹2,500 crore to ₹5,000 crore range as "large".

It said Vyoma.AI, via LTN Compute, secured a multi-year engagement with an inference infrastructure provider to deploy an additional NVIDIA B300 GPUs at its Chennai Data Center.

The infrastructure will power the inference infrastructure provider's AI-native platform, enabling it to train, fine-tune and deploy specialized AI models for high performance inference at commercial scale. This development strengthens India's AI infrastructure while supporting the growing global demand for advanced compute, the company said.

The integrated AI factory will bring together hyperscale data center infrastructure, accelerated computing, high-performance networking, ultra-low latency interconnects, high-throughput parallel storage and comprehensive AI infrastructure operations to enable efficient deployment of demanding AI workloads, it added.

L&T said the AI factory is being developed at Vyoma.AI's Chennai campus, envisioned as a gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure hub. Its Phase 1 is designed for 250 MW, supported by 150 MVA power infrastructure readiness, providing a scalable foundation for future capacity expansion, it said.

"Our Chennai AI factory will deliver the scale, performance and resilience required to accelerate global AI innovation and strengthen India's position as a leading hub for next-generation computing," SN Subrahmanyan, the chairman and managing director of L&T, said.

Shares of Larsen & Toubro are trading 1.1% lower on Monday at ₹4,161.6. The stock is up 14% in the last one month and as a result, has reversed all of its year-to-date losses as well.

data.title: Rupee retreats, Goldman calls it a 'port of stability' in AI storm
data.description:
By Jaspreet Kalra

The Indian rupee retreated after touching a seven-month high on Monday, pausing a five-day rally driven by robust portfolio inflows amid a rotation away from crowded AI trades, with Goldman Sachs describing the unit as a "port of stability in the AI storm."

The rupee rose to a peak of 92.44 in early trades, its strongest level since April, before reversing course; it was last quoted at 92.8825, compared with its previous close of 92.67.

It is on course for a monthly gain of over 2% — its best since March 2025 — shored up by a foreign investor rush into local stocks that has poured $13 billion into Indian equities over November already.

On Monday, a burst of corporate dollar buying weighed on the rupee after it rose in early trading, with traders pointing to such demand also coming from two large conglomerates.

The rupee's early gains also pushed it into overbought territory, per a key momentum indicator.

"While we remain sceptical that spot appreciation at this pace can extend given the need to rebuild external reserve buffers, there seems to be a greater commitment to allowing more two-way volatility in the currency," analysts at Goldman Sachs said in a note.

India's foreign exchange reserves (INFXR=ECI) declined to a three-month low of about $705 billion as of November 13, according to data released on Friday.

"In this type of global markets backdrop, the rupee should continue to be a port of stability in the AI storm," the note added.

In addition to gaining against the dollar, the rupee has also strengthened about 4% against the British pound and the euro alongside a 3% gain against the Japanese yen over November so far.

data.title: GME Stock Heads For A Green Month: Wall Street Reportedly Sees A New Growth Story Beyond The Meme-Stock Hype
data.description:
Key points:
  • StoneX analyst Mike Hickey sees a 24% upside potential for GME stock. 
  • Roaring Kitty's return with a Cat Mario post failed to fetch a meme stock rally.
  • Dan Ives said GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is shifting the business toward collectibles. 

GameStop (GME) stock is on track for a green month as Wall Street sees a future beyond meme-stock hype. StoneX initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating, betting on booming collectibles sales, store reopenings and a potential boost from “Grand Theft Auto VI.”

GameStop stock edged 0.5% higher overnight Sunday. The stock has been gaining for three straight weeks and has rallied 10% so far this month.

A New Growth Strategy Takes Shape For GameStop 

According to a MarketWatch report, StoneX analyst Mike Hickey believes the retailer's investment appeal has changed. Instead of depending on ‘meme stock’ buzz, the company could benefit from rising demand for collectibles and gamers purchasing new hardware to enjoy blockbuster releases.

“It’s a real company, and it’s trading at what we think is a very undervalued price,” Hickey said. He added that StoneX previously viewed the stock negatively but has since changed its position, explaining that the speculative trading phase has run its course.

StoneX recently began covering GameStop with a ‘Buy’ rating and a $33 price target, implying a 24% upside potential from the stock’s last close. The firm sees green shoots in the retailer's decision to reopen selected U.S. locations, following years of store closures.

“There’s really no other stock that you can buy that gives you that much exposure to collectibles,” said Hickey.

Roaring Kitty's Influence On GME Appears To Be Fading

The latest test of GameStop's meme-stock appeal came Thursday, when Keith Gill, better known as Roaring Kitty, posted a picture of Cat Mario on his X account after nearly two years of silence. Gill helped turn GameStop into a meme stock in 2021.

This time, however, the reaction was relatively muted. GameStop stock only advanced 1.5% on Thursday, followed by a 1% drop on Friday.

Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., believes GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is reshaping the retailer around collectibles while improving its operating efficiency.

“This is no longer a meme stock; it’s in the process of becoming a new and improved story,” Ives said. GameStop’s second-quarter collectibles revenue surged 57%, accounting for 45.1% of the company's total sales.

GME Stock: Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bullish’ with a 96% increase in message volume over the past week.

A user said, “What most people seem to be missing is that this is a much more solid company RN. The roaring meow never mattered for long-term holders.” The user also added that GameStop has expanded its collectibles business, which has grown rapidly in popularity.

Another user said, “All of those who say that RC will dilute as soon as this pump is in denial - I very much doubt he will want to devalue all the board buys that happened in the last month and a half.”

GME stock has gained 32% year-to-date.

data.title: Halder Venture to acquire stake in India's InQube
data.description:
Indian agricultural company Halder Venture (BSE: 539854) has signed binding agreements to acquire a 52% stake in agri-technology firm InQube Technologies for INR301.6mn ($3.25mn), the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 20.

The deal would take Halder Venture beyond its existing farming business into agricultural software and carbon credit projects. InQube, founded in April 2022, is a small operation. Its turnover fell to INR5.65mn in the 2025-26 financial year from INR12.68mn a year earlier, according to the filing.

Halder Venture signed a share subscription and share purchase agreement and a shareholders's agreement on November 20. The board had approved the investment and a term sheet earlier, as disclosed on February 13.

Once the conditions precedent in the agreements are met, the company will own 52% of InQube's equity on a fully diluted basis, and the target will become its subsidiary. Payment will come as a combination of cash and shares. Halder Venture has allowed up to 24 months from the signing of the agreements to close the transaction. It added that no government or regulatory approvals are required.

InQube operates a cloud-based, multilingual enterprise resource planning platform for the farm sector and runs projects that generate carbon credits. Its business is confined to India. It reported turnover of INR7.10mn in 2023-24.

Halder Venture said the purchase would give it technology tools to make the agricultural value chain more efficient. It would also give the company a route into selling carbon credits and promoting sustainable farming practices.

The company expects the acquisition to build an end-to-end value chain and open new sources of revenue. The filing said the acquisition does not currently count as a related party transaction, but InQube will become a related party after completion.

data.title: Explained - How the mega M&A deal impacts both APL Apollo Tubes and Tata Steel
data.description:
The mega two-stage transaction between APL Apollo Tubes Ltd., and Tata Steel Ltd., have sent shares of both the companies down by up to 16% on Monday, November 23. It has also raised several crucial questions for investors across both companies and the broader supply chain.

How Does The Deal Impact Tata Steel?

For Tata Steel, the transaction presents near-term financial headwinds. With the steelmaker’s net debt already standing at ₹91,423 crore, committing significant capital to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo puts additional strain on its balance sheet.

Furthermore, the deal has been struck at an expensive valuation of roughly 27 to 28 times EV/EBITDA based on FY27 estimates, a steep multiple compared to traditional steelmakers, which typically trade at single-digit multiples. Investors will closely watch how Tata Steel manages its leverage while integrating these downstream assets.

Impact Of The Transaction on APL Apollo Tubes?

On the flip side, the deal acts as an immediate positive trigger for APL Apollo Tubes. In the near term, the open offer price of ₹2,301 per share provides strong valuation support and clear upside visibility for minority shareholders.

However, looking beyond the transaction, a major strategic question remains: can APL Apollo continue to command its rich, consumer-style valuation multiples once promoter Sanjay Gupta steps away? Under his leadership, the company earned a significant market premium through aggressive execution and category creation. But under Tata Steel’s parentage, the market may begin valuing it closer to a traditional steel subsidiary.

What Happens To Other APL Group Listed Entities?

With Gupta exiting APL Apollo, the market focus has quickly shifted to the two other listed companies under his promoter group - SG Mart and SG Finserve, and what this liquidity event means for their future growth trajectories.

Shares of SG Mart surged 9% on Friday as investors anticipated renewed promoter focus and potential capital deployment. The board of the company will be meeting later this week to consider a fund raising proposal. The company currently commands a market capitalization of close to ₹14,000 crore, with promoter holding standing at 57.88%.

Similarly, the group’s financial services arm, SG Finserve, holds a market capitalization of around ₹5,500 crore with a promoter stake of 56.95%, positioning it as another key vehicle where Gupta could channel his bandwidth and capital going forward.

Potential HRC Sourcing Shifting

Finally, the change in ownership carries major ripple effects for upstream steel suppliers. As India's largest structural steel tube manufacturer, APL Apollo is one of the biggest consumers of Hot Rolled Coils (HRC) in the country.

Once Tata Steel assumes majority control, APL Apollo’s raw material procurement strategy could undergo a significant shift. A gradual pivot toward captive HRC sourcing from Tata Steel would pose a direct volume risk to incumbent third-party suppliers—most notably JSW Steel and ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India), potentially altering competitive dynamics across the domestic flat steel market.

What Is The Mega Transaction?

Tata Steel will be acquiring up to 26.38% stake in APL Apollo Tubes for an all-cash transaction of 15,510.6 crore. The company will acquire another 26% stake from public shareholders of APL Apollo Tubes through a mandatory open offer, whose price of ₹2,301.4 per share, is a premium to APL Apollo's closing price last Friday.

The deal is supposed to be executed in three tranches, of which, the first tranche of Tata Steel buying 10% stake in APL Apollo via block deals was executed earlier in the day, where APL Apollo shares worth nearly ₹5,500 crore changed hands in a block deal.

The remaining two tranches will be completed on or before March 31, 2028.

Shares of APL Apollo Tubes are trading 16% lower on Monday at ₹1,788. The stock has turned negative on a year-to-date basis. Shares of Tata Steel are also down 6.5% on Monday at ₹167.

data.title: Maybank Third-Quarter Profit Rose on Stronger Fee Income
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Malayan Banking's third-quarter net profit rose 4.7%, beating market expectations, driven by stronger core fee income and higher net fund-based income.

Malaysia's largest lender by market capitalization said Monday that quarterly net profit was 2.74 billion ringgit, equivalent to $666.2 million. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha had expected 2.71 billion ringgit.

Net interest income was 3.13 billion ringgit, down from 3.27 billion ringgit a year ago, while noninterest income fell to 2.38 billion ringgit from 2.46 billion ringgit, Maybank said.

data.title: Why Did NVDA, NFLX, ORCL Slip To 52-Week Lows Last Week?
data.description:
Key points:
  • NVDA stock closed down 14% on Friday as investors worried about the company’s future amid former CEO Jensen Huang’s exit. 
  • NFLX stock was down nearly 3% at close on Friday amid pressure from its slowing revenue growth and rising competitive concerns. 
  • ORCL stock fell nearly 9% at close last week amid a wider rout in the tech sector, with the company’s massive AI data center capital expenditures and heavy debt accumulation exerting further pressure. 

Shares of Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Netflix Inc. (NFLX), and Oracle Corp. (ORCL) plunged to 52-week lows on Friday amid growing leadership concerns, slowing growth, and increasing AI debt concerns.

NVDA stock closed down 14% on Friday as Wall Street and Main Street worried about the company’s future amid former CEO Jensen Huang’s exit.

NFLX stock was down nearly 3% at close on Friday amid pressure from its slowing revenue growth and rising competitive concerns.

ORCL stock fell nearly 9% at close last week amid a wider rout in the tech sector, with the company’s massive AI data center capital expenditures, heavy debt accumulation, and negative free cash flow exerting further pressure.

Nvidia Struggles With Leadership Transition Woes

NVDA shares fell to a 52-week low of $124.50 on Friday as concerns around its leadership grew after former CEO Jensen Huang was ousted from the company amid reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia appointed Colette Kress as interim CEO, effective Nov. 12.

Over the weekend, The Fly reported that Phillip Securities had lowered its price target on Nvidia to $225 from $300 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares. The revised target still implies an upside of about 79% from the stock’s last close.

The firm cited risks from the company's leadership transition and business strategy beyond fiscal 2029 for the target cut. Growth rate assumptions for Nvidia are unchanged, it said, as it sees no material impact to supply at the moment.

Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday backed Huang’s return as the chipmaker’s CEO. In a post on Truth Social, he said, “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.”

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NVDA stock was ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing. Shares of the company have plunged more than 32% year-to-date.

Netflix Grapples With Slowing Revenue Amid Growing Competition

NFLX stock tumbled to a 52-week low of $56.56 on Friday as a slowdown in its revenue growth, downgraded advertising expectations, rising competitive pressures, and potential high-cost bidding for major live events ratcheted up selling pressure.

Netflix has seen its year-over-year revenue growth gradually decelerate, dropping from about 17.6% in late 2025 down to roughly 11.8% in the third quarter of 2026. Its fourth-quarter revenue growth projection is 11.5%.

Meanwhile, in its latest earnings report, management cut back its 2026 advertising revenue forecast down to roughly $2.7 billion, from an earlier target of $3 billion, driven by delays in ad-tech rollout and partner deals.

Reports that the company is eyeing major bids, such as an estimated $1.5 billion-plus play for U.S. rights to the 2030 men's World Cup, have also raised questions about future content costs and margin pressure.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NFLX stock was ‘extremely bearish’ at the time of writing. Shares of the company have plunged more than 39% in 2026.

Oracle Faces Pressure Amid Broader Tech Selloff

ORCL stock slumped to a 52-week low of $100.25 on Friday as a broader selloff in the technology and AI sectors dragged its price lower.

The company has also been grappling with concerns regarding its massive AI data center capital expenditures and heavy debt accumulation.

To fund its infrastructure expansion, Oracle has raised significant debt, surpassing about $150 billion to $170 billion, and executed large equity and note offerings, such as a recent $20 billion funding package, which has diluted earnings.

Despite Oracle’s multi-hundred-billion-dollar contract backlog, investors worry whether those long-term commitments will translate into actual free cash flow. However, the company reaffirmed its $664 billion cloud backlog and financial targets last week, announcing that it has secured all the funding required to fulfill its infrastructure commitments.

Anthropic’s recent IPO also drained liquidity from markets, straining technology shares, including Oracle’s.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ORCL stock was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing. Shares of the company have tumbled more than 47% so far this year.
